title: MCP vs CLI: Benchmarking Tools for Coding Agents
author: Mario Zechner (Pi Agent creator)

key_discoveries.title: MCP bypasses Haiku malicious-command detection — 35-55x token savings
key_discoveries.detail: CLI tools trigger Claude Code's bash security scanner (claude-3-5-haiku) on every invocation. 10 CLI runs consumed 1.3-2M Haiku tokens. 10 MCP runs consumed ~35K Haiku tokens. MCP bypasses the bash tool entirely, eliminating the security-check round trip. Architecturally significant for cost modeling of Pi supervisor tool calls.
key_discoveries.action: Factor Haiku bypass into MCP vs bash-tool cost models in Pi supervisor; prefer MCP for high-frequency tool calls

key_discoveries.title: Single-tool MCP pattern (one tool, action parameter) — validated empirically
key_discoveries.detail: terminalcp exposes one MCP tool with an 'action' parameter covering start/stop/stdin/stdout/stream/list/version commands. Zechner cites the (now-removed) Anthropic docs warning about tool count limits degrading agent performance. Our pi-mcp-adapter already uses this pattern — this is independent empirical validation.
key_discoveries.action: Enforce single-tool MCP design pattern for all new Pi extensions; audit existing tools for consolidation opportunities

key_discoveries.title: terminalcp — PTY-based tmux alternative with MCP + CLI, by Pi Agent creator
key_discoveries.detail: terminalcp uses node-pty + xterm.js for PTY emulation, runs as a persistent daemon, communicates via Unix socket. It is architecturally similar to pi-interactive-shell but with both MCP and CLI interfaces. Cleanly handles TUI apps (debuggers, REPLs, vim, htop). GitHub: https://github.com/badlogic/terminalcp
key_discoveries.action: Catalogue terminalcp as a Pi ecosystem tool; evaluate as complement/replacement for our tmux dependency in Pi supervisor

key_discoveries.title: screen fails on TUI tasks — avoid for interactive TUI agent control
key_discoveries.detail: GNU screen scored 0/10 on the OpenCode TUI model-switching task. It cannot handle the interactive dialog navigation required by modern TUIs. tmux, terminalcp MCP, and terminalcp CLI all scored 100%. Avoid screen for any agent task requiring TUI interaction.
key_discoveries.action: Remove screen from consideration in any terminal control architecture; prefer tmux or PTY-native solutions

key_discoveries.title: tmux wins on simple tasks, MCP wins on complex TUI tasks
key_discoveries.detail: For LLDB debug and Python REPL (simple), tmux is cheapest ($0.373-$0.716 avg) due to training data familiarity. For OpenCode TUI navigation (complex), terminalcp MCP saves 39% over tmux ($0.671 vs $1.105 avg). The crossover point is task complexity / back-and-forth frequency.
key_discoveries.action: Use tmux for simple terminal tasks; consider MCP-based PTY tool for complex multi-step TUI interactions

key_discoveries.title: Eval framework pattern — Claude as judge for agent output analysis
key_discoveries.detail: Zechner's eval framework: (1) spawn fresh Claude Code per run with clean config, (2) capture full ANSI terminal stream, (3) Claude Code reads outputs and judges success/failure/improvements per tool, (4) second pass ranks all tools with analysis. Each run costs ~$0.37-$1.47. Framework can run in parallel.
key_discoveries.action: Adopt this eval pattern for benchmarking our own Pi supervisor tool configurations; reusable for future agent tool comparisons

tools_to_catalogue.name: terminalcp
tools_to_catalogue.reason: By Pi Agent creator; PTY-based tmux alternative with MCP+CLI; single-tool MCP design pattern; handles TUI apps (debuggers, REPLs); potential tmux dependency replacement
